title: Amnesty International: RSF Committed Crimes Against Humanity, Ethnic Cleansing in El Fasher
detail: Amnesty International published a 200+ page report, 'City Under Siege, Children Under Fire: Rapid Support Forces' Crimes Against Humanity in North Darfur,' at a launch event in Nairobi on July 1, 2026. Based on 247 interviews (208 survivors), 89 open-source videos, and satellite imagery covering early 2024 through El Fasher's October 2025 fall, the report documents murder, forcible transfer, torture, rape, sexual slavery, enslavement, extermination, and persecution targeting the Zaghawa ethnic group, including mass executions of hundreds of people at a 57km berm network during the final RSF offensive — one survivor described seeing 'more than 1,000 dead bodies.' The report names alleged commanders including Al-Fateh Abdullah Idris ('Abu Lulu') and Maj. Gen. Gedo Hamdan Ahmed Mohamed ('Abu Shouk'). Amnesty Secretary-General Agnès Callamard called it 'a war on civilians' and 'a stain on the conscience of humanity,' urging an immediate nationwide ceasefire and an international protective force.

title: RSF Razes Six Zaghawa Villages Near Tine, North Darfur, Displacing Thousands
detail: A large RSF force attacked six Zaghawa-inhabited villages along the Ambara-Tine road near the Chad border beginning Wednesday, July 1, 2026: Qarboura, Oruwa, Um Marahik, Kourbia, Abu Leiha, and Ana Baji. RSF vehicles fired artillery through homes; Oruwa and Ana Baji were reportedly burned entirely, water wells were destroyed, and livestock looted. Survivor Issa Ibrahim, 35, told AFP dozens of RSF vehicles stormed his village of Um Marahik: 'They sent artillery through homes, they burned to the ground and people died on the street with no one to bury them.' By Friday, July 3, more than 3,500 people had been displaced from Wadi Fungo village (Um Baru locality) alone, per IOM, with thousands more fleeing toward Chad. The attacks followed days after Joint Forces gains at Abu Qamra and Kulbus, suggesting a retaliatory dynamic. The UN separately reported that more than 200 children were killed in Darfur in the first six months of 2026.
